# PhysicsPalm

**Class** · namespace `VRFramework.Interaction.Runtime` · assembly `VRFramework.Interaction.Runtime` · [view source](https://git.cie-group.cz/vr-framework/vrf4/core/-/blob/main/Runtime/Scripts/Interaction/PhysicsPalm.cs#L22)

What the hand's own body is resting on, so the palm can press with it.

The palm's counterpart to [`PhysicsFinger`](/api/vrframework-interaction-runtime/PhysicsFinger). A finger has a body of its own to
hear collisions on; the palm's body is the [`PhysicsHand`](/api/vrframework-interaction-runtime/PhysicsHand), and this sits beside it
to listen. Put there by [`PhysicsFingers`](/api/vrframework-interaction-runtime/PhysicsFingers) rather than written into the hand,
because the hand does not run outside play mode and this has to - a press is measured headless
under `Physics.Simulate`, and without `ExecuteAlways`no contact is ever heard there.

Only declared surfaces are noted, and every one of them the hand is on, each by its own
collider. A palm is wide: bottoming out a button mounted on a panel that is a surface too, it
rests on both at once, and one note that kept whichever collider spoke last lost the button
under the palm still pressing it. Nothing is refused either: unlike a finger, the hand is
meant to be stopped by everything it meets.

```csharp
[ExecuteAlways]
[AddComponentMenu("")]
[RequireComponent(typeof(Rigidbody))]
public class PhysicsPalm : MonoBehaviour
```
